strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real limitations of sequential search in RAG systems with compelling examples
Thoughtful and principled automatic dataset construction pipeline with verification of necessity for parallel/sequential hops
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 diverse benchmarks with multiple strong baselines and meaningful metrics (AUC)
Strong and consistent empirical improvements (+15.9 F1 on FanOutQA, +11.5 F1 on BrowseComp-50) with good scaling analysis
Effective analysis of model behavior through evidence coverage curves and performance scaling with search budget
Clear presentation with well-designed visualizations and good motivation
weaknesses: Dataset quality concerns: only 27% trajectory generation success rate (773/1987 questions) with insufficient analysis of failure modes and whether low-quality trajectories persist
Model backbone mismatch in experiments: HybridDeepSearcher uses Qwen3-8B while baselines use Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, creating confounds that weaken controlled comparison
Limited dataset analysis: only 2,111 training examples with no ablations on component contributions, dataset size scaling, or special token effects
Insufficient error analysis: no qualitative failure case comparisons, per-category breakdowns, or investigation of when parallel search hurts performance
Evaluation reliability issues: heavy reliance on MBE which is known to be unreliable, and BrowseComp-50 is cherry-picked (50 questions solvable by OpenAI o3 in 5 minutes)
Reproducibility limitations: HDS-QA generation depends on Google's API responses (not reproducible), no code/dataset release plans mentioned
Limited methodological novelty: core idea is straightforward, architecture is standard fine-tuning with special tokens, most contribution is dataset-based rather than algorithmic
Missing ablations and analysis: no statistical significance testing, no context length reduction validation, no analysis of parallel query execution limits, no human evaluation of trajectories

strengths: Clear motivation and problem identification with effective illustrative examples
Creative automatic dataset construction pipeline with reasonable quality controls (4-step process)
Comprehensive evaluation across 5 diverse benchmarks with multiple metrics (F1, MBE, turns, AUC)
Strong empirical improvements on specific benchmarks (FanOutQA +15.9 F1, BrowseComp-50 +11.5 F1)
Good reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, and prompts
Thorough evidence coverage analysis (Table 3) demonstrating search capability improvements
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution is supervised fine-tuning on a new dataset without methodological or architectural innovation for parallelization
Dataset quality concerns: 27% success rate without human evaluation; no validation of question coherence, answer trajectory validity, or data quality
Unfair experimental setup: inconsistent backbone models (Qwen3-8B vs Qwen2.5-7B), no controlled ablations, and unfair advantage from training on the same reasoning patterns
Unclear source of improvements: no evidence that improvements come from parallelization specifically rather than general multi-hop supervised training or data scale
Latency claims lack support: 'search turns' does not equal wall-clock latency; actual inference time not measured; marginal turn reduction (1.9) may not translate to meaningful speedup
Problematic evaluation: MBE metric uses same model family (Qwen3-32B) for evaluation; AUC is non-standard; missing standard metrics like EM; no significance testing or error bars

Generalization issues: dataset from Natural Questions, evaluated on very different tasks (FRAMES, BrowseComp); BrowseComp-50 subset selection introduces bias; synthetic parallelization may not reflect natural parallelizable queries
Missing critical comparisons: no fine-tuning of baselines on HDS-QA; no comparison with concurrent parallel-query work (Tan et al. 2025, Zhao et al. 2025); limited baseline diversity
Insufficient analysis: no ablation studies on dataset components; no systematic error analysis; no wall-clock latency measurements; no out-of-distribution evaluation
Incomplete related work discussion and missing ethical considerations regarding environmental cost and data bias

Strong and consistent empirical results across five diverse benchmarks: +15.9 F1 on FanOutQA, +11.5 F1 on BrowseComp-50, highest AUC scores, demonstrating both effectiveness and efficiency gains

Thoughtfully designed automated dataset construction pipeline: leverages 'People Also Ask' for diversity, ensures hybrid-hop questions genuinely require both parallel and sequential reasoning, generates 2,111 validated trajectories

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple metrics (F1, MBE, AUC, evidence coverage), diverse baselines, extended analysis with budget constraints, scaling studies showing performance improves with additional resources
Excellent presentation and reproducibility: well-written paper with clear figures, complete prompts in appendix, detailed case studies, full implementation details enabling reproduction

Demonstrates clear scalability benefits: Figure 4-5 show consistent performance improvements as search budget increases, with effective utilization of parallel queries reducing turns while maintaining accuracy
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: core contribution is dataset construction rather than methodological or architectural innovation; model uses straightforward fine-tuning with added special tokens
Missing critical ablation studies: no ablations on dataset size impact, reasoning tag design, trajectory diversity, or single-epoch training decision; unclear which factors drive improvements

Dataset quality and scale concerns: only 1,987 questions with 27% success rate; 2,111 training trajectories is relatively small; heavy reliance on LLM-generated trajectories could introduce systematic biases; no human evaluation of quality

Evaluation setup limitations: BrowseComp-50 is a biased subset (pre-selected as solvable by o3 in 5 minutes); different model backbones for baselines complicate comparison; no statistical significance testing

Incomplete analysis and missing error characterization: no error analysis of failure modes; no investigation of when/why model chooses parallel vs. sequential queries; limited discussion of failure cases; no insight into decision-making patterns

Generalization and scope limitations: evaluation restricted to web-search QA tasks; unclear if approach generalizes to other domains requiring planning; dataset leverages Natural Questions + Google's 'People Also Ask' with limited scope

Dataset reproducibility concerns: relies on Google's 'People Also Ask' feature which may change or become unavailable; unclear if exact reproduction would yield identical dataset; limited discussion of generalization

Incomplete baseline comparisons: concurrent parallel search methods (Tan et al. 2025; Zhao et al. 2025) mentioned but not directly compared; limited clarification of differences from multi-query baselines like DeepResearcher and RAG-R1

Thoughtfully designed HDS-QA dataset construction pipeline with demonstrated diversity in parallel width and sequential depth (Appendix B)
Consistent improvements across all benchmarks with strong test-time scaling curves (up to 3-4× gains)
Useful ablation studies including single-query variant, model scale variations (4B/32B), and summarizer ablations
Improved evidence coverage (Table 3) demonstrating better retrieval of necessary documents

weaknesses: Limited novelty: Core contribution is dataset construction + standard fine-tuning with no architectural or algorithmic innovation; the model is just Qwen3-8B fine-tuned on supervised data

Dataset quality concerns: Only 38.9% (773/1987) question generation success rate; small scale (2,111 examples, typically 10k-100k+); all questions follow single template limiting reasoning diversity; potential distribution bias from NQ + People Also Ask sources

Insufficient mechanism analysis: No rigorous ablation isolating whether improvements come from parallel breadth, explicit aggregation, or simply training on longer examples; missing error breakdown and failure mode analysis

strengths: Clear problem identification: Demonstrates that existing search methods plateau despite increased budgets, with well-motivated motivation and examples
Novel dataset contribution: HDS-QA with 2,111 examples explicitly combining parallel and sequential reasoning addresses a gap in existing training data
Comprehensive evaluation: 5 benchmarks, multiple metrics (F1, Acc, AUC), diverse baselines, showing consistent improvements (+15.9 F1 on FanOutQA)
Test-time search scaling: Compelling demonstration that the method continues improving with more turns/calls while competitors plateau (Figure 1, 3)
Thorough empirical analysis: Evidence coverage (Table 3), robustness to evidence requirements (Figure 4), ablations (Table 4), and model scale experiments
Strong reproducibility: Complete prompts in appendices, detailed experimental setup, qualitative case studies enabling reproduction
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: Core contribution is dataset supervision rather than new reasoning mechanisms; model is standard fine-tuning of Qwen3-8B
Dataset quality concerns: Only 38.9% pass@4 suggests many questions lack correct trajectories; no human evaluation of trajectory quality or reasonableness
Evaluation setup bias: BrowseComp† is curated to questions solvable by o3 within 5 minutes (arbitrary criterion); unequal budgets for method vs baselines (MT limit vs 10 turns)
Unclear mechanism: Why supervised learning outperforms GRPO is underexplored; GRPO analysis uses only binary rewards; Qwen2.5-7B baseline on HDS-QA performs comparably
Inconsistent scaling gains: Strong scaling on BrowseComp† but more modest on MuSiQue/FRAMES; initial performance with few calls sometimes lower than baselines
Limited analysis of when method works: No characterization of which question types benefit from hybrid search or failure modes; only evaluated on QA tasks
Comparison fairness: Different summarizer models across experiments; incomplete engagement with concurrent parallel search work; no inference cost analysis
